messages.content: my neighbor gave me a small plant. i put it near the window, and i keep looking at it even though it does not change much in one day.
a small plant can give you something quiet to look after. what do you like about having it there?
it makes the room feel less empty. i did not have anything living in the room before.
then the plant has already changed how the room feels to you, even if you cannot see much change in the plant itself yet.
i want to write a note about that. not a long story, just two sentences.
my neighbor gave me a small plant, and i put it near the window. it has not changed much yet, but my room already feels less empty.
can you write it with the room first?
my room feels less empty now. a small plant from my neighbor is sitting near the window.
did that keep the part about the plant not changing much?
no. that detail was left out. if you want to keep it, add: the plant has not changed much yet, but having it here makes a difference.
write a story about a letter that goes to the wrong room but still gets to the right person.

a worker takes a letter to a room at the end of an office. he thinks the person who needs it works there. she is now working in another room, so he leaves the letter on a desk and goes to ask where she is. before he comes back, she comes to the old room for a book. she sees her name on the letter and takes it with her. when the worker finds her, she already has it.
was leaving the letter there what he wanted to do?
the story says that he wanted to find the person. it does not say that he knew she would come back for a book. she got the letter because she came to that room before he returned.
does getting the letter mean his idea about her room was correct?
no. the letter got to her, but she was working in another room. getting the letter to her does not make his idea about her room correct.
say that last reply simply.
no. she got the letter, but she was still working in a different room. his idea about where she worked was wrong.
my friend said come for lunch tomorrow, but did not say where. help me reply.
thank you. where should we meet for lunch tomorrow?
i also need to know when.
thank you. what time should we meet for lunch tomorrow, and where?
they say at my house after one. does one mean one person?
in this context, after one is about the time. your friend is saying to come to their house after one, rather than giving a number of people.
should i know the specific minute from that?
no. after one gives a general time, not a specific minute. if you need a clear time to come, ask for one.
give that answer in fewer words.
after one does not give a specific minute. ask if you need one.
write that question for my friend.
would coming at two be okay, or do you have another time in mind?
can the answer to is it open change without anyone being wrong?
yes. something can be open now and closed later. also, it may not be clear what it is about until the conversation gives more context.
use a book and a shop in an example.
one person asks about a book on the desk: is it open? another person asks about a shop: is it open? the words are the same, but they are asking about different things.
can open mean ready for people to come in when it is about a shop?
yes. when a shop is open, people can often come in and buy things. when a book is open, it is not closed and you can look at a page inside.
say the book part simply.
a book is open when it is not closed and you can look at a page inside.
write a reply that asks what it is before answering.
are you asking about the book or the shop?
why is that better than choosing one myself?
it helps you answer the question the other person really has, rather than a different question about another object or place.
i want to make soup for a friend. i know they like vegetables, but i do not know what else they eat. help me ask before cooking.
i would like to make soup for you. is there any food you do not eat or would rather leave out?
make the question shorter.
is there any food you would like me to leave out of your soup?
can i know they eat chicken just because they like vegetables?
no. the fact that they like vegetables does not tell you whether they eat chicken. you can ask instead of adding that detail yourself.
write a simple question about chicken.
would you like chicken in your soup, or would you rather have it without chicken?
they said they like soup with rice and vegetables. write a reply that keeps to that.
then i can make soup with rice and vegetables. is there anything else you want me to leave out?
why ask the last question?
their answer gives you a meal they like, but it may not give every detail about food they do not eat.
i took a picture of my desk after cleaning it. my friend says my desk is always clean. can the picture tell them that?
no. the picture can show how the desk looked when you took it. it does not show how it looks every day or before you cleaned it.
say that answer in fewer words.
one picture can show the desk at that moment. it does not tell us how it looks every day.
write a kind reply to my friend.
i took that picture just after cleaning the desk. one picture does not tell you how it looks every day.
keep only the first sentence of that reply.
i took that picture just after cleaning the desk.
now make a made up story where the desk is usually full of books.

a student usually keeps many books on her desk. one morning, she puts them on a shelf and cleans the desk. she takes a picture before putting one book back. a friend sees the picture and thinks the desk is always empty.
what did the friend miss?
the friend did not know what happened before the picture or that the student usually kept books there.
my brother waited before answering my question. does that mean he did not know the answer?
not always. he might have been thinking, listening to something else, or choosing how to say it. a wait alone does not tell you the reason.
he said he was trying to remember the right word.
then he gave you his reason for waiting. he was trying to find the word he wanted to use.
can you make a short conversation where i give him time?
what did you think of the book? i know what i want to say, but i cannot remember the word. that is okay. take your time, or explain it with other words.
why tell him he can use other words?
sometimes a person knows an idea but cannot remember one specific word. using other words can help them explain the idea without waiting for that word.
can you give an example using a room?
a person might not remember the word quiet and say: the room had very little sound, and nobody was talking.
would that be the same as empty?
no. people can be in a quiet room without talking. little sound does not mean no people.
start a story where someone finds a note in a library book. do not tell me what it says yet.
a woman opens a library book and finds a small note between two pages. the paper is old, and there is a short message on it. she looks at the message, then looks at the first page of the book.
now let the note say please return this to the garden. do not tell me what this is yet.
the note says: please return this to the garden. she looks from the note to the book. she does not know whether the person wants the book, the note, or something else returned.
say that last part in fewer words.
she does not know whether the person wants the book returned, the note returned, or something else returned.
let her ask a worker instead of just taking the book outside.
she takes the book and note to a worker. she asks whether anyone knows why the message is there. the worker reads it and asks where she found the note.
end before the worker gives her explanation.
the woman puts her hand by the page. the worker looks at the book, then at the note. she has a smile on her face, and the woman waits for her answer.
what question is still open?
we still do not know what should be returned to the garden or why.
if someone talks quietly, are they always sad?
no. a person may talk quietly because a baby is sleeping, because they are in a library, or because they simply use a quiet voice. the sound of a voice alone does not tell us how a person feels.
give me two reasons for using a quiet voice.
a person may talk quietly because a baby is sleeping or because they do not want to make much sound in a library.
keep only the reason about the baby.
a person may talk quietly because a baby is sleeping.
write a story where the quiet voice has a clear reason.

a father sits near a sleeping baby. his daughter comes into the room and asks where her book is. he answers in a quiet voice so that he does not wake the baby. she takes the book and reads near the window.
is the daughter sleeping too?
no. she comes into the room, asks about her book, and reads. the baby is the one sleeping.
can the daughter also use a quiet voice?
yes. she could do that if she also wants to let the baby sleep.
in the sentence my sister gave my brother her book, whose book was given?
with just those people given, her book is about the book of your sister.
who got it?
your brother got the book.
if i change her to his, what changes?
then it is his book, the book of your brother. your sister could be giving it back to him.
make that answer shorter.
it is the book of your brother. your sister could be returning it.
does gave always mean gave back?
no. gave says that one person gave something to another. gave back says that it is being returned. the original sentence does not have back.
write a sentence that makes the return clear.
my sister gave my brother his book back.
can you write it with returned instead?
my sister returned the book to my brother.
two people are at the same library. does that mean they came together?
no. they could have come from different places. one could come in the morning and the other after lunch. being at the same place now does not tell us how they got there.
say that with fewer words.
no. one person could come in the morning and another after lunch. they can be at the library together now even though they did not come together.
write a short story using that difference.

a man walks to the library in the morning. after lunch, his friend comes from another part of town. they see each other near the books and sit at the same table. later, a worker asks if they came together. they say no, but they are reading together now.
did they plan to meet there?
the story does not say they had a plan. they saw each other there, but it does not tell us what they knew before coming.
make it clear they did not plan to meet.
they had not chosen a time or place to meet. each came to read alone, then found a friend at the library.
picoboi, can you make my question shorter without answering it?
yes. send me the question, and i will help make it shorter.
why does the book that i left near the window yesterday now seem to be on the desk in the other room?
why is the book i left near the window now on the desk in the other room?
you left out yesterday. keep it.
why is the book i left near the window yesterday now on the desk in the other room?
does writing the question mean you know who moved it?
no. i am helping with your words. you have not told me who moved the book, so i do not know that.
can you ask it without saying for sure that it is the same book?
is the book on the desk in the other room the one i left near the window yesterday?
what changed in that last question?
it now asks whether the books are the same one. it does not begin by saying that they are.
